hints: Describe mass as an intrinsic property of a body, not as the gravitational force acting on it.
walkthrough: Mass is the property of a body that resists a change in its motion.
Equivalently, mass may be described as the quantity of matter in a body.

ai_rubric.observable: States that mass resists changes in motion or identifies it as the quantity of matter in a body.

hints: Link the equal-and-opposite interaction forces to momentum changes over the same collision time.
walkthrough: During the collision, block A exerts a force on block B and block B exerts an equal-magnitude, opposite-direction force on block A.
Force is the rate of change of momentum, F = Δp / Δt.
Both forces act for the same contact time, so the momentum changes are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the blocks exert equal-magnitude, opposite-direction forces on each other during the collision.
Links force to rate of momentum change and notes that the common contact time makes the momentum changes equal and opposite.

hints: Choose one direction as positive and give the initially left-moving block a negative velocity.
Write total momentum before the collision equal to total momentum after it, keeping the masses as 3M and M.
walkthrough: Take motion to the right as positive. Initially, the total momentum is (3M)(0.40) + M(−0.25).
After the collision, it is (3M)(0.20) + Mv.
Solving gives v = 0.35 m s⁻¹, so block B moves to the right at this speed.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses momentum as mass multiplied by velocity for the blocks.
Forms a signed total-momentum equation before and after the collision.

hints: For bodies moving towards each other, their speeds add; when they move in the same direction, subtract their speeds.
walkthrough: Before collision, the blocks move in opposite directions, so their relative speed of approach is 0.40 + 0.25 = 0.65 m s⁻¹.
After collision, both blocks move right. Block B has speed 0.35 m s⁻¹ and block A has speed 0.20 m s⁻¹.
Their relative speed of separation is 0.35 − 0.20 = 0.15 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the relative speed of approach as 0.65 m s⁻¹.
Calculates the relative speed of separation as 0.15 m s⁻¹.

hints: For an elastic collision, compare the relative speeds before and after the collision.
walkthrough: The relative speed of approach is 0.65 m s⁻¹, whereas the relative speed of separation is 0.15 m s⁻¹.
For an elastic collision, these relative speeds would be equal.
They are not equal here, so the collision is inelastic.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the collision as inelastic because the relative speed of separation is less than and not equal to the relative speed of approach.
